stem: An ordinary annuity pays Rs 5,000 at the end of each year for 3 years. The rate of interest is 10% per annum. What is the future value of this annuity?  [Given: (1.1)^3 = 1.331]

per_option_rationale.rationale: Simply summing the three payments Rs 5,000 x 3 = Rs 15,000 ignores interest accumulation on earlier payments.
Treating the annuity as an annuity-due (payments at the beginning of each period) gives FV_due = 16550 x 1.1 = Rs 18,205, which is wrong for an ordinary annuity.
Erroneously adding 10% of the total nominal sum Rs 15,000 once gives Rs 15,000 + Rs 2,000 = Rs 17,000; this misapplies the compounding formula.

explanation: Future value of an ordinary annuity: FV = A x [(1+i)^n - 1] / i. With A = 5000, i = 0.10, n = 3: FV = 5000 x (1.331 - 1) / 0.10 = 5000 x 3.31 = Rs 16,550.

explanation_sections.punchline: An ordinary annuity's future value accumulates interest on each payment from the period it is made - use FV = A[(1+i)^n - 1]/i.
explanation_sections.lesson: Ordinary annuity payments are at period-end; if payments were at period-start (annuity-due), multiply by (1+i).
explanation_sections.timing: 50 seconds. One formula application with the provided hint. Trap: option 1 = simple sum, no interest.
